events.title: Michelangelo is born
events.description: The future painter, sculptor and poet was born in Caprese, in the Republic of Florence. He went on to create the statue of David and the Sistine Chapel ceiling.
events.significance: Michelangelo became one of the defining figures of the Italian Renaissance. His work still shapes ideas of artistic genius.

events.title: The Alamo falls
events.description: After a 13-day siege, Mexican forces under General Antonio López de Santa Anna stormed the Alamo mission in San Antonio, Texas. They defeated the Texan defenders.
events.significance: "Remember the Alamo" became a rallying cry in the Texas Revolution. The battle became a lasting symbol of resistance in American memory.

events.title: Mendeleev presents the periodic table
events.description: Russian chemist Dmitri Mendeleev presented his system for organizing the chemical elements by atomic weight and recurring properties to the Russian Chemical Society.
events.significance: His table brought order to chemistry and left gaps for elements not yet discovered. It remains a cornerstone of modern science.

events.title: Ghana gains independence
events.description: The Gold Coast became the independent nation of Ghana, ending British colonial rule. Kwame Nkrumah led the country into independence.
events.significance: Ghana was the first sub-Saharan African country to win independence from European colonial rule. Its example inspired independence movements across the continent.
